selection: 40 frozen classic excerpts plus 8 fixed excerpts from one 2006 story. Convenience preference pilot, not a representative benchmark.
qualification: This compares a short request, planned craft generation and a longer craft+QA workflow. The workflow uses more calls; an effect cannot be attributed to the skill text alone. Same-model reviews can share mistakes. Historical public works may have been present in model training; runtime isolation cannot erase that prior knowledge.

modern_batch.source_context: Complete English story, excluding foreword and licence text. No published Russian input.
modern_batch.limits: One contemporary author and one story. Not representative of contemporary literature. Russian attribution and licence are asserted by two digital mirrors; original Computerra publication was not inspected.

cohorts: Up to 20 passages; eligible modern passages are included first, then classic works. No repeat overlapping excerpts.
voting_eligibility: Four fragments have exactly equal whitespace-normalized baseline and reviewed outputs. All outputs are preserved, but those fragments are excluded from UI cohorts and the vote allowlist to avoid arbitrary method attribution. This is deterministic duplicate handling, not selection by quality or preference. The same duplicate rule applies to the modern batch.
interpretation: Preferences for these frozen outputs only. Era, author and genre are confounded; do not attribute differences between works to skills. Results can be filtered by work.
